name: Helix Biosystems Pulmonary Resection Bellows
description:
The Pulmonary Resection Bellows is a compact, accordion-framed pneumatic device designed to maintain respiratory function in patients whose pulmonary musculature has been compromised by trauma, toxin exposure, or combat-grade neurotoxic agents. It attaches via a sealed oral-nasal interface and a pair of intercostal anchor clips, mechanically driving inhalation and exhalation cycles calibrated to the patient's blood-oxygen readout through a small embedded biosensor. In field conditions, it can sustain a flatlined respiratory system for up to six hours without recharge.

What distinguishes the Bellows from earlier mechanical ventilators is its adaptive rhythm engine — a low-power analogue processor that modulates breath cadence in response to detected movement, ambient noise, and patient heart rate variability. This means a downed operative being carried through a firefight won't asphyxiate due to positional changes or jostling. The device also features a one-way toxin filter membrane rated for most aerosolized chemical agents found in GLMZ's contested industrial zones.

The Bellows is standard-issue in Helix Biosystems extraction teams and has found a devoted secondary market among deep-sewer runners and tunnel-breach specialists who work in environments with chronically compromised air quality. Street medics refer to it as 'The Deacon' — something that keeps you breathing when you have no business doing so.

specifications.interface: Sealed oral-nasal mask with intercostal anchor clips (sizes A–D)
specifications.compatible_patients: Human baseline, most cyberframe configurations with intact thorax

tactical_use: Deployed immediately following chest trauma, drowning events, or neurotoxin exposure that collapses diaphragm function. A medic can attach the Bellows in under forty seconds. Once secured, the patient can be moved, carried, or dragged without interrupting respiratory support. Operators also use it prophylactically before breaching chemically contaminated spaces, running it at low support alongside natural breathing to reduce lung fatigue during prolonged toxic exposure.
cultural_context: Among extraction crews and tunnel runners, carrying a Bellows is considered a mark of professional seriousness — it signals that you expect casualties bad enough to need sustained life support in the field, and you're prepared for it. In the poorer outer wards, bootleg Bellows units with degraded filter membranes circulate widely, used by residents living near Ouroboros Energy's poorly sealed exhaust stacks. Helix's licensing requirements are widely resented; unlicensed possession in corporate-controlled zones carries fines that price the device out of reach for those who need it most.
known_users: Long-haul courier crews transiting contaminated freight corridors
story_hooks: A shipment of Bellows units with deliberately degraded filter membranes has been routed to outer ward free clinics — someone is profiting from the failures, and the bodies are starting to pile up.
A player character wakes up post-operation with a Bellows attached and no memory of how they got there — the device's biosensor log contains encrypted movement data from the last six hours.

A Helix Biosystems licensing inspector is found dead in a tunnel with a bootleg Bellows still running on her face, keeping her technically alive despite catastrophic brain death — someone wants to delay the official time of death.
A tunnel runner community has jury-rigged a network of salvaged Bellows units into a crude collective air filtration system for their hab-block — Helix's legal team has arrived to dismantle it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact accordion-frame pneumatic device resembling a miniaturized bellows or concertina pump. The central body features a ribbed, compressible silicone accordion core flanked by two rigid frame panels. A sealed oral-nasal interface mask extends from the top like a medical snorkel, while two curved metal intercostal anchor clips protrude from the sides. The overall aesthetic is industrial-medical: functional, modular, purposeful.
physical_description.dimensions: 22 cm tall × 14 cm wide × 9 cm deep when collapsed; expands to roughly 16 cm depth when in use. Handheld to chest-mounted scale.
physical_description.weight_description: 1.4 kg assembled—light enough for one-handed field deployment but substantial enough to feel robust. Typically worn on a patient's sternum or carried in a field medic's kit.
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum frame (ribbed side panels), medical-grade silicone accordion core, stainless steel anchor clips, polycarbonate sensor housing.
physical_description.finish: Brushed aluminum with satin-matte silicone. The accordion displays subtle ribbed texture. Anchor clips have a burnished metallic sheen. The sensor window is clear polycarbonate with faint holographic Helix Biosystems branding etched into it.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray frame with deep ocean-blue silicone accordion. Accent colors: sterile white on the oral-nasal interface, emergency red on the filter cartridge access panel. Helix Biosystems logo in chrome.
physical_description.interface_elements: A small LCD readout (roughly 4 cm diagonal) on the upper frame displays blood-oxygen saturation, breath rate, and battery status. Two tactile buttons for manual mode override and power. A sealed rotary filter-cartridge access port on the lower housing. A bio-sensor LED array (green/yellow/red) indicating system status. Quick-release silicone clips lock the mask interface in place.
distinctive_features: Accordion silicone core with visible ribbing—suggests mechanical flexibility and durability
Dual intercostal anchor clips with rubberized grip pads—designed to grip rib-cage without damaging tissue
Integrated bio-sensor window with faint holographic readout overlay (O2 %, HR variability graph)
Filter cartridge access panel marked with Class IV hazmat symbol in embossed relief
Power indicator LED array that cycles from green (nominal) to amber (low battery) to red (critical)
Weathered patina typical of field-used medical gear—scuffed metallic finish, faint blood-stain residue on clips, worn silicone surfaces
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Helix Biosystems logo (chrome stylized double-helix) centered on upper panel. Serial number and batch code laser-etched on frame. Regulatory stamps: GLMZ Medical Authority approval mark, Class IV toxin filter certification, biocompatibility rating.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained unit shows light surface wear: micro-abrasions on aluminum from field carry, slight discoloration on silicone from repeated sterilization, faint dust residue in the accordion grooves. The mask interface may bear traces of previous patient contact (cleaned but not pristine). Battery indicator glowing amber or green depending on use state.
